findings.title: Exit code change from 4 to 3 for recreate upgrade breaks documented contract and existing automation
findings.body: The PR changes RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 (and introduces FEATURE_DISABLED = 4). This is a breaking change to the exit-code contract of the `update-compatibility check` command: any existing CI/CD pipeline or script that was written against the already-released behavior (where exit code 4 meant 'rolling upgrade not possible') will now misinterpret the result. Exit code 3 previously had no meaning for this command, and 4 is now reused for a different condition (feature disabled). The docs in docs/guides/server/update-compatibility.adoc are updated to match the new values, but the change silently invalidates automation built against the previous release. If this command has already shipped in a released version, the exit code for 'recreate upgrade' must not be changed; a new code should be added instead (e.g., keep 4 for recreate and use 5 for feature-disabled), or the change must be clearly called out as breaking in release notes.

findings.title: Feature check runs before config validation, so --features=rolling-updates is never actually honored for the check itself
findings.body: In `run()`, the code checks `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES)` before `validateConfig()` is called. The `--features` option is a runtime configuration option that is only applied to the Profile during configuration processing (which happens in validateConfig()/the Quarkus config phase). At the point of the check, the Profile reflects only the persisted/optimized build-time configuration, not the `--features=rolling-updates` CLI flag passed on the command line. This means a user running `kc.sh update-compatibility check --file=x.json --features=rolling-updates` on a server where the feature is not enabled in the build will still get 'feature not enabled' and exit code 4, even though they explicitly passed the flag — contradicting the documentation (docs/guides/templates/kc.adoc) which shows the command being run with `--features=rolling-updates` appended. The feature gate therefore cannot be satisfied via CLI at all for non-optimized invocations, making the documented usage in kc.adoc and update-compatibility.adoc incorrect. The check should either be performed after configuration is applied, or the feature flag should be read from the parsed CLI options directly.

Since the Profile is only updated with CLI-provided feature flags during configuration processing, a user who runs `kc.sh update-compatibility metadata --features=rolling-updates` (exactly as documented in docs/guides/templates/kc.adoc line 53 and docs/guides/server/update-compatibility.adoc line 63) on a default build will always be rejected with 'The preview feature rolling-updates is not enabled' and exit code 4. The documented command therefore cannot work as written unless the feature was enabled at build time, which contradicts the purpose of the docs showing the flag being passed at invocation time.

findings.title: No test verifies the exit code for the feature-disabled path (exit code 4)
findings.body: The new test `testFeatureNotEnabled` asserts only the error message via `cliResult.assertError(...)`, but never asserts the exit code. The whole point of introducing `CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` is to give automation a machine-readable signal (documented in update-compatibility.adoc exit-code table). Without asserting `cliResult.exitCode() == 4`, a regression that returns a different code (e.g., the generic picocli error code 1 or 2) would not be caught. The test should assert the exit code equals `CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED` for both the `metadata` and `check` subcommands. Additionally, there is no test asserting exit code 3 for the recreate/incompatible path (testWrongVersions only asserts the error message), leaving the changed exit-code contract untested.

findings.title: Test parameterization with null strategy no longer exercises the feature-disabled path, and the feature is now always enabled
findings.body: In `createInitialDeployment`, when `updateStrategy == null` the method returns early (line 105-107) before the `ROLLING_UPDATES` feature is enabled (lines 112-115). Previously the null-strategy case configured the update spec via the `unsupported` stanza; now the null case gets neither an update spec nor the feature. The test names (`testImageChange-{0}`, `testCacheMaxCount-{0}`) and the comment on line 64 ('changing the image to non-existing will always use the recreate upgrade type') suggest the null case is meant to represent the default/legacy behavior, but with the feature flag now being a hard requirement for the operator's update strategies (per the new CAUTION in advanced-configuration.adoc: 'the feature rolling-updates must be enabled. Otherwise, the Keycloak Operator will fail'), the null-strategy deployment may fail outright rather than exercise the intended default path. The test does not assert that the initial deployment actually becomes ready before the upgrade is triggered, so a failure of the initial deployment would surface as a confusing timeout. Either the null case should also enable the feature (to test default strategy behavior with the feature on), or a separate test should verify the operator fails when the feature is missing — currently neither is covered.

However, the NOTE block immediately below (lines 461-466) says 'During this preview stage, the update strategy defaults to mimicking Keycloak 26.1 or older behavior' and the table lists `<not set>` (default) as a valid value that 'Mimics Keycloak 26.1 or older behavior'. findings.title: CAUTION says commands fail without the feature, but the documented command examples pass --features=rolling-updates which (per the code) does not satisfy the gate
findings.body: The guide's CAUTION block (lines 12-16) states the feature 'must be enabled. Otherwise, the commands will fail.' Yet every command example in the guide (via the kc.adoc macro, line 63 and 83) appends `--features=rolling-updates` at invocation time. As implemented in UpdateCompatibilityCheck/UpdateCompatibilityMetadata, the feature check reads the Profile before CLI options are applied, so passing `--features=rolling-updates` on the command line does not enable the feature for the check — the command will still fail with exit code 4. The documentation therefore instructs users to do something that does not work. The docs should state that the feature must be enabled at build time (e.g., `kc.sh build --features=rolling-updates`) or the code should be fixed so the CLI flag is honored (see related finding). Until one or the other is resolved, the guide is incorrect.

findings.title: New ROLLING_UPDATES preview feature gates operator and CLI behavior but has no versioned key or dependency declaration, and preview features are auto-enabled by the preview profile
findings.body: ROLLING_UPDATES is declared as Type.PREVIEW, which means it is automatically enabled for all users running with `--profile=preview` (see isEnabledByDefault, line 316-325). This feature gates significant operational behavior: the Keycloak Operator's update strategies (documented as causing the operator to fail if not enabled) and the update-compatibility CLI commands. Auto-enabling an operator-affecting feature for every preview-profile user is a broad blast radius for a preview feature; users who enable the preview profile for unrelated features (there are many other PREVIEW features) will silently get the rolling-updates behavior change in the operator. Consider whether this should be PREVIEW_DISABLED_BY_DEFAULT (which exists in the Type enum precisely for 'Preview features, which are not automatically enabled even with enabled preview profile') so that it must be explicitly enabled, matching the docs' emphasis that it 'must be enabled'.
